title: Cross out, mark, and what the class ticked
items: Cross out an option you’ve ruled out: right-click it, long-press it on a phone, or Shift + its letter. It isn’t graded.
Mark a question to see it again (the Mark button, or M). Your marked questions wait on the Tonight card and on each module page.
After checking a question: how many in the class ticked each option on their first try.

title: Quest exams, short or long
items: Exam mode on the quest now asks how long: 20 questions like the midterm, 50, or all of them. A short one takes questions from every lecture of the quest, in proportion.

title: Digestive surgery midterm quest
items: The 100 past questions on the seven lectures of the digestive surgery midterm (Wednesday 14 October) in one place: appendicitis, peritonitis, groin hernias, hydatid cyst of the liver, caustic ingestion, stomach and esophageal cancer. With a countdown, progress by lecture and seals to earn.

title: Dermatology: 7 more professor’s questions
items: Seven questions from the professor’s dermatology list that weren’t on the site yet: varicella, shingles, retinoids, acne, syphilis and Kaposi. Nobody had marked answers for them, so they were answered from the S5 lectures.

title: Answers checked against the lectures
items: The answers that looked doubtful were checked against the S5 lectures, and the ones that didn’t match were corrected. Checked answers now say “Checked against lecture”.

title: Respiratory midterm 2026–2027
items: Today’s respiratory midterm, all 15 questions as they were given, with proposed answers. Practise it, or take it as a timed exam.

title: Studying together
items: After you check a question, see how the class did on its first try, once enough of you have answered it. A question most people miss is worth a second look.

The class sky on the homepage: do 10 questions in a day and your star rises into that day’s sky. The more of you there are, the more constellations you form together, starting with the Little Bear around the Labubu’s North Star. Hover a star to see who it is, or hide yours anytime.

title: Themes to earn
items: Two new looks for the Den, earned by studying: Codex, an illuminated manuscript in parchment, gold leaf and vermilion, when one lecture reaches Solid on its diagnostic; and Blood moon, blackletter and crimson with castles and bats, with your first full moon. Each comes with its own lettering and sounds.
See them under Themes on the homepage, with what each asks and how close you are. Tap a locked one for a short preview.

title: Comets and the moon
items: Comets: a question you miss comes back the next day, then after 3, 7 and 14 days, until it sticks. Catch tonight’s from the Tonight card on the homepage (with an account).
The moon: do 5 questions in a day and that night counts; 14 nights make a full moon, and a night off only pauses it.
Before checking a question you can say whether you’re sure. The weak spots page then tells you how good your instinct is.

title: Accounts
items: Sign in at the top of the homepage, with Google or an email and a password. Exam mode, weak spots and quests now need an account; practising questions stays open to everyone.
Signed in, your answers, weak spots and exam marks follow you between your phone and your laptop as you go.

title: Practise by lecture
items: Every past question is now filed under the lecture it comes from, from this year’s slides. On a module page, switch to By lecture to practise one lecture at a time, in course order.
Weak spots now diagnose each lecture (tuberculosis as its four lectures, for example), and exams group your results by lecture.

title: Weak spots, and exam mode everywhere
items: Any past exam set can be taken in exam mode as it was given, and any module as a mock exam the size of a midterm, a mock or the finals.
Weak spots: try 8 questions of a topic and it gets diagnosed, with your mark on it, what your wrong ticks cost, and every fact to fix with the lecture’s why.

title: Exam mode
items: Take the quest as a timed exam: its 48 questions in a random order, one minute each, marked out of 20.

All the right answers ticked give the point, at least half of them half a point, and any wrong tick nothing for that question. After handing in, go through every question with its answer and explanation.

title: Sounds
items: Picking, checking and moving between questions now click and chime (right answers climb with your streak), with a vibration on phones. The speaker in the quiz bar turns the sound off.

title: Constellations
items: In the quest, a question asked again with the same propositions counts once, as a constellation. Hover over it to see where it came up, or do all its stars one by one.

title: Explanations
items: Every question on the respiratory midterm's six topics now explains why each proposition is right or wrong, from the lectures.

title: Corrected questions
items: Some questions were corrected: a few answers and typos.

title: Flagging and feedback
items: Every question has a Report a mistake link that flags it to the Labubu, and Ask the Labubu on the homepage takes your ideas for the site.

title: Update log
items: New questions are listed here when they’re added, and the homepage shows how many are new.

title: Respiratory midterm quest
items: The 60 past questions on the six midterm topics in one place, with a countdown, progress by topic and seals to earn.

title: Most repeated questions
items: The 224 questions asked in two or more exam sets, ranked, plus a Repeated only option in each module.

title: Topic search
items: Search by topic in English or French, with abbreviations and typos, and narrow it down to signs, diagnosis or treatment.

title: Midterms 2025–2026
items: Practice by module or by exam, check your answers, and see where each answer comes from, with notes and explanations.
